name: Heterocyclic Chemistry
tagline: Synthesis, reactivity, and pharmaceutical applications of ring systems.
seo_title: Heterocyclic Chemistry — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Heterocyclic Chemistry on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in heterocycle synthesis, drug scaffolds, natural products and functional materials.

definition.lead: Heterocyclic chemistry studies ring molecules that contain at least one atom other than carbon, most often nitrogen, oxygen or sulfur.
definition.body: These rings are everywhere in life and medicine: the bases of DNA, haem, chlorophyll, vitamins and most small-molecule drugs. Replacing one ring carbon with a nitrogen changes basicity, shape and the way a molecule binds its target.

branches.name: Five-membered rings
branches.summary: Pyrrole, furan, thiophene, imidazole and their relatives.
branches.example: Four pyrroles form the porphyrin ring of haem and chlorophyll.

branches.name: Six-membered rings
branches.example: Cytosine, thymine and uracil are pyrimidines.

branches.name: Fused ring systems
branches.summary: Two or more rings sharing a bond.
branches.example: Indole in serotonin; purine in caffeine and adenine.

branches.name: Heterocycles in drugs
branches.summary: Rings that tune how a drug binds, dissolves and is metabolized.

branches.name: Ring synthesis
branches.example: The Hantzsch pyridine and Fischer indole syntheses.

branches.name: Aromaticity
branches.summary: How heteroatoms share or withhold their lone pairs.
branches.example: Pyrrole's lone pair is part of its aromatic sextet, so it is barely basic.

branches.name: Alkaloids & natural products
branches.summary: Nitrogen-containing ring compounds made by living organisms.

branches.name: Heterocycles in materials
branches.summary: Rings in conductive polymers, dyes and light emitters.

timeline.title: Rings from coal tar
timeline.text: Friedlieb Ferdinand Runge finds pyrrole and quinoline in coal tar.
timeline.why: Coal tar became the first source of heterocycles.

timeline.title: Pyridine
timeline.text: Thomas Anderson isolates pyridine from oil obtained by heating bones.
timeline.why: Today one of the most common rings in approved drugs.

timeline.title: Indole
timeline.text: Adolf von Baeyer obtains indole while studying the dye indigo.
timeline.why: The ring at the heart of tryptophan and serotonin.

timeline.title: The Hantzsch synthesis
timeline.text: Arthur Hantzsch builds pyridine rings from simple carbonyl compounds and ammonia.
timeline.why: Still used to make calcium-channel blocker drugs.

timeline.title: The Fischer indole synthesis
timeline.text: Emil Fischer makes indoles from arylhydrazines and ketones.
timeline.why: One of the most used ways to build indoles.

timeline.title: The Paal–Knorr synthesis
timeline.text: Carl Paal and Ludwig Knorr make furans and pyrroles from 1,4-diketones.
timeline.why: A simple, general route to five-membered rings.

timeline.title: Penicillin's ring
timeline.text: Dorothy Hodgkin's X-ray work confirms penicillin's four-membered β-lactam ring.
timeline.why: Explained how the antibiotic works and guided new ones.

timeline.title: Base pairing
timeline.text: The DNA double helix pairs purines with pyrimidines.

timeline.title: Triazoles by click
timeline.text: Copper-catalysed azide–alkyne cycloaddition is reported by the Meldal and Sharpless groups.
timeline.why: Made 1,2,3-triazoles one of the easiest rings to build.

quiz.q: Which of these is a heterocycle?
quiz.explain: Pyridine is benzene with one CH replaced by nitrogen.

quiz.q: Why is pyrrole a much weaker base than pyridine?
options: Its nitrogen lone pair is part of the aromatic π system
It has no nitrogen atom at all
It is not aromatic, so it cannot be protonated
It already carries a positive charge
quiz.explain: Protonating pyrrole's nitrogen would destroy its aromaticity.
Adenine and guanine are purines; cytosine and thymine are pyrimidines.
The indole ring is a benzene fused to a pyrrole.

quiz.q: What ring system is at the core of caffeine?
quiz.explain: Caffeine is a methylated purine, like a cousin of adenine and guanine.

quiz.q: What is penicillin's key reactive ring?
quiz.explain: The strained ring acylates the bacterial enzyme that builds cell walls.
Thiophene has sulfur; pyrrole has nitrogen.

quiz.q: The Fischer indole synthesis builds indoles from…
options: Benzene and ammonia over a catalyst
quiz.explain: An acid-promoted rearrangement then closes the ring.

options: Furan joined to a benzene ring
quiz.explain: Its name comes from the tobacco plant, Nicotiana.

quiz.q: Haem and chlorophyll are built around…
options: A porphyrin: four pyrrole units in a large ring
A single benzene ring with metal substituents
A crown ether that wraps the metal ion
quiz.explain: The central metal is iron in haem and magnesium in chlorophyll.

quiz.q: Roughly what share of FDA-approved small-molecule drugs contain a nitrogen heterocycle (2014 analysis)?
quiz.explain: A 2014 analysis found 59% of unique small-molecule drugs contain at least one.
